symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings (target-like pattern) on older lower leaves.
Yellowing (chlorosis) halo surrounding leaf lesions.
Premature defoliation starting from the bottom of the canopy upward.
Sunken, dark leathery lesions at the stem end of fruits.
tomato_early_blight.cause: Fungal pathogen Alternaria solani surviving on crop residue and solanaceous weeds.
cultural_controls: Prune and safely dispose of infected lower leaves at first sight; do not compost.
Mulch soil with clean straw or plastic to prevent soil splash onto lower foliage.
Implement a 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (e.g., legumes or cereals).
biological_controls: Apply bio-control agents such as Trichoderma viride or Trichoderma harzianum to soil/foliage.
Foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis bio-formulations during early disease onset.
Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) as an organic antifungal repellent.
monitoring: Scout lower leaves twice weekly during warm, humid weather.
Inspect leaf undersides for concentric ring lesions after rain events.
water_management: Switch to drip irrigation to keep foliage completely dry.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation and avoid field operations while foliage is wet.
tomato_early_blight.chemical_advisory: If threshold (>5% lower canopy defoliation) is reached, standard protective contact fungicides (e.g., copper-based formulations or mancozeb) may be evaluated. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds and resistant or tolerant tomato varieties.
Ensure adequate plant spacing (60 cm x 45 cm) for canopy ventilation.
tomato_early_blight.source_note: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Tomato IPM Extension Guidelines & TNAU Agritech Portal.

symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale-to-brown lesions on leaves and stems.
White fungal-like fuzzy growth on the underside of leaves during cool, humid mornings.
Rapidly browning and collapsing foliage; field appears frost-damaged.
Firm, dark brown greasy lesions expanding across green or ripening fruit.
cultural_controls: Immediately rogue out and destroy severely blighted plants outside the field boundary.
Eliminate volunteer tomato and potato plants from surrounding bunds and ditches.
Promote air movement across rows by staking and pruning side shoots.
biological_controls: Preventive foliar application of bio-agents like Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L).
Trichoderma harzianum soil enrichment to suppress overwintering oospores.
monitoring: Daily inspection of leaf undersides and stems during foggy, overcast, or continuous rainy periods.
Monitor local late-blight forecast alerts issued by regional agromet advisories.
water_management: Ensure rapid surface water drainage and avoid standing water in furrows.
Strictly refrain from overhead irrigation to curtail leaf wetness duration.
tomato_late_blight.chemical_advisory: Late blight progresses destructively within 48 hours. Preventive contact or systemic fungicides (e.g., copper oxychloride, metalaxyl-mancozeb combinations) are recommended under persistent cold-wet conditions. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Plant certified resistant hybrids and maintain strict sanitation.
Avoid planting tomato immediately adjacent to potato crops.
tomato_late_blight.source_note: CPRI Shimla & ICAR Extension Bulletin on Solanaceous Late Blight Management.

symptoms: Pale green to yellowish patches on upper leaf surfaces.
Olive-green to grayish velvety fungal mold growth on corresponding lower leaf surfaces.
Infected leaves wither, turn brown, and drop prematurely.
cultural_controls: Ventilate polyhouses or dense canopies to lower ambient relative humidity.
Prune lower suckers and dense foliage to facilitate natural air circulation.
Disinfect support trellises and stakes before every planting cycle.
biological_controls: Foliar spray with Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
Application of fermented organic bio-wash or cow urine solution (1:10 dilution).
monitoring: Inspect lower and middle foliage undersides weekly.
Monitor relative humidity levels inside the canopy using an aspirating psychrometer or hygrometer.
water_management: Irrigate only at soil level in early morning so humidity does not spike overnight.
Maintain raised beds to prevent excessive soil moisture accumulation.
tomato_leaf_mold.chemical_advisory: If fungal mold exceeds 10% canopy coverage, protective copper or sulfur-based sprays may be used where humidity cannot be controlled. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Select resistant varieties with Cf resistance genes.
Avoid over-fertilization with nitrogen, which produces excessively dense foliage.
tomato_leaf_mold.source_note: University Extension IPM Database & ICAR-IIHR Tomato Disease Management.

symptoms: Numerous small (2-3 mm) circular spots with dark brown margins and gray or tan centers.
Tiny black pinhead-like pycnidia specks visible inside lesion centers.
Progressive yellowing and dropping of lower leaves, exposing fruit to sunscald.
cultural_controls: Strip and safely dispose of infected foliage below the lowest fruit cluster.
Apply clean straw mulch to keep rain from splashing fungal spores from the soil.
Deeply plow under crop residues immediately after final harvest.
biological_controls: Foliar application of Trichoderma viride formulation at 5g/L.
Neem seed kernel extract (5%) spray at the first appearance of leaf spots.
monitoring: Carefully inspect the bottom 30 cm of foliage weekly after rain or heavy dew.
Check for black fruiting bodies in spots using a hand lens.
water_management: Always use drip irrigation; avoid splash-generating overhead irrigation.
Water crops early in the morning so incidental wetting dries quickly.
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.chemical_advisory: Fungicide options such as chlorothalonil or copper hydroxide can prevent secondary spread if applied early. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for at least 2 seasons.
Maintain clean borders free from solanaceous nightshade weeds.
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.source_note: FAO Plant Production and Protection Series & TNAU Expert System for Tomato.

symptoms: Small, dark, greasy or water-soaked circular spots on leaves.
Spots turn purplish-brown with yellow halos and ragged margins.
Crabby, blister-like raised scabby spots on green fruits.
Extensive leaf blighting and blossom drop during warm rainy weather.
cultural_controls: Never work in wet tomato fields; human handling spreads bacterial ooze rapidly.
Remove severely infected plants and safely incinerate or deep-bury them.
Disinfect all pruning shears, stakes, and crates with 10% bleach solution.
biological_controls: Bacteriophage treatments targeting Xanthomonas where commercially accessible.
Seed treatment and root dip with Pseudomonas fluorescens bio-agent.
monitoring: Regularly inspect leaves and fruits for greasy water-soaked spots after rainstorms.
Examine nursery seedlings before field transplanting.
water_management: Eliminate overhead watering and shield seedlings from heavy rain splash.
Improve drainage ditches to prevent standing water near root zones.
tomato_bacterial_spot.chemical_advisory: Copper hydroxide mixed with mancozeb offers preventive suppression. Streptomycin sulfate sprays may be advised under specific agricultural extension supervision. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Use certified disease-free, hot-water-treated seed (50°C for 25 minutes).
Do not save seeds from infected fields.
tomato_bacterial_spot.source_note: University of Florida IFAS Extension & ICAR Bacterial Disease Protocol.

symptoms: Pinpoint brown spots expanding into circular lesions with light brown centers.
Dark concentric rings resembling target boards on leaves and stems.
Severe premature defoliation in lower and middle canopies.
Deep, sunken brown crater-like rot on ripening fruit.
cultural_controls: Prune the lower suckers and bottom leaves to prevent ground contact.
Provide sturdy stakes and trellising to lift plant foliage off the soil.
Destroy infected crop residues after harvest to interrupt fungal life cycles.
biological_controls: Foliar spray with bio-fungicides based on Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma species.
Neem cake soil amendment at transplanting to enhance plant resilience.
monitoring: Inspect inner lower canopy where humidity lingers longest.
Check green fruits for small circular depressions.
water_management: Drip irrigation only; avoid high-pressure hose spraying.
Maintain wide row spacing to allow sunlight penetration and leaf drying.
tomato_target_spot.chemical_advisory: Broad-spectrum protective fungicides (e.g., azoxystrobin or mancozeb) can be applied preventively during prolonged warm-humid periods. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Maintain a 3-year rotation away from cucurbit, solanaceous, and legume hosts.
Use pathogen-tested seeds and clean nursery potting mix.
tomato_target_spot.source_note: CABI Invasive Species Compendium & ICAR Plant Pathology Advisory.

symptoms: Severe upward cupping, rolling, and reduction in leaf size.
Interveinal yellowing (chlorosis) and pale green young foliage.
Marked plant stunting with a bushy, erect 'bonsai' appearance.
Flower abortion and failure to set marketable fruit.
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.cause: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV), transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
cultural_controls: Erect yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps per acre) to monitor and mass-trap adult whiteflies.
Install 40-50 mesh insect-proof netting over seedling nursery beds.
Rogue out and destroy infected viral plants immediately to prevent whitefly acquisition.
biological_controls: Conserve or release natural predators such as Chrysoperla carnea (green lacewing) and ladybird beetles.
Foliar spray of entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana or Lecanicillium lecanii (5g/L).
Spray 5% neem seed kernel extract or 1% horticultural mineral oil to repel whitefly vectors.
monitoring: Inspect under surfaces of young leaves daily for tiny whitefly adults and nymphs.
Check yellow sticky trap counts every 48 hours.
water_management: Ensure balanced soil moisture to avoid water-stress which aggravates whitefly attacks.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer, which attracts succulent-feeding whitefly populations.
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.chemical_advisory: Viruses cannot be cured with chemical sprays; chemical intervention focuses strictly on vector management. Systemic insecticides (e.g., imidacloprid, thiamethoxam, or cyantraniliprole) may be recommended for vector suppression during early nursery stages. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Grow TYLCV-resistant or tolerant hybrids (e.g., US 440, NS 501, etc.).
Grow 3 border rows of tall non-host barrier crops like maize, sorghum, or pearl millet.
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.source_note: World Vegetable Center (AVRDC) & ICAR Whitefly Management Technical Bulletin.

symptoms: Mottling of light and dark green patterns on leaves (mosaic pattern).
Distortion, blistering, and stringy 'shoestring' narrowing of leaflets.
Stunted growth and poor overall canopy vigor.
Brown internal browning and uneven ripening of fruits.
tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Tomato Mosaic Virus (ToMV), mechanically transmitted through sap, hands, tools, and seeds.
cultural_controls: Workers must wash hands with soap and water or 20% skimmed milk before touching plants.
Strictly prohibit tobacco smoking or chewing near tomato fields (tobacco carries virus strains).
Rogue and safely bag infected plants without letting them brush against adjacent healthy crops.
biological_controls: Treat seeds with trisodium phosphate (10% TSP) solution or heat therapy prior to sowing.
Soil application of beneficial mycorrhizae and Pseudomonas to enhance plant vigor.
monitoring: Scout young transplants 14 to 21 days after field planting for mosaic mottling.
Inspect foliage whenever pruning or trellising is performed.
water_management: Use automated drip systems to minimize physical movement of workers through wet fields.
tomato_mosaic_virus.chemical_advisory: No chemical fungicides or viricides are effective against plant viruses. Chemical control is strictly restricted to vector control if aphids or thrips are present. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Plant certified ToMV-resistant tomato cultivars.
Sterilize all cutting tools, stakes, and trays with 10% trisodium phosphate or bleach.
tomato_mosaic_virus.source_note: EPPO Global Database & ICAR Virus Disease Advisory.

symptoms: Vibrant green leaves with uniform coloration and no necrotic spots or chlorosis.
Firm, well-developed stems and robust growing tips.
Normal flower cluster development and healthy fruit set.
tomato_healthy.cause: No pathogen detected; optimal crop physiological condition.
cultural_controls: Continue standard good agricultural practices (GAP).
Maintain routine weeding and mulching around base stems.
Ensure proper plant staking and ventilation.
biological_controls: Routine preventive soil drench or root application with Trichoderma and biofertilizers.
Maintain flowering border crops (marigold, mustard) to encourage predatory insects.
monitoring: Maintain bi-weekly routine crop scouting for early detection of pests or blight.
Monitor soil moisture levels and local weather forecasts.
water_management: Continue regulated drip irrigation based on crop evapotranspiration needs.
Keep soil evenly moist, avoiding sudden cycles of extreme drought and over-watering.
tomato_healthy.chemical_advisory: No chemical fungicides or pesticides are necessary. Maintain preventive bio-immunization. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Maintain balanced N-P-K and micronutrient (calcium, boron) supply.
Keep field borders clean of weeds.
tomato_healthy.source_note: Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Tomato, FAO & ICAR.

symptoms: Small dark brown to black spots with concentric rings on older bottom leaves.
Leaf tissue between veins turns yellow and dies, causing premature vine senescence.
Brown corky dry rot in potato tubers with sunken margins.
cultural_controls: Remove volunteer potato sprouts and bury infected haulms after dehaulming.
Adopt a minimum 3-year rotation excluding tomato, pepper, and eggplant.
Maintain adequate potassium and nitrogen fertility to delay crop senescence.
biological_controls: Foliar application of Trichoderma viride or Bacillus subtilis.
Neem seed kernel extract (5%) spray during early crop stages.
monitoring: Inspect lower leaves starting 45 days after emergence.
Scout following periods of alternating dew and warm dry days.
water_management: Irrigate during early morning so vines dry before evening.
Maintain uniform furrow or sprinkler irrigation to avoid plant stress.
potato_early_blight.chemical_advisory: Contact protective fungicides like mancozeb or chlorothalonil may be applied at early bloom if leaf spots exceed economic threshold. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers.
Ensure proper earthing up to protect tubers from spore wash.
potato_early_blight.source_note: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) Shimla IPM Package.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark brownish-purple patches on leaves and petioles.
Delicate white fungal down on the lower surface of leaves under wet conditions.
Stem lesions causing entire vines to collapse within days.
Reddish-brown granular dry rot spreading inward beneath tuber skin.
cultural_controls: Perform haulm destruction (dehaulming) 10-12 days prior to harvest to safeguard tubers.
Rogue out and bury seed-tuber cull piles before the cropping season starts.
Earth up potato ridges deeply (15-20 cm) to create a soil buffer preventing spore wash to tubers.
biological_controls: Prophylactic foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L).
Bio-control formulation of Trichoderma harzianum applied at ridge planting.
monitoring: Track daily late blight decision support system (CPRI JHULSACAST or regional agromet bulletins).
Inspect low-lying, shaded areas of the field daily during overcast, wet spells.
water_management: Do not irrigate if rain is forecasted or when relative humidity remains above 85%.
Facilitate rapid furrow drainage.
potato_late_blight.chemical_advisory: Prophylactic spray of mancozeb before disease appearance, followed by systemic mixtures (e.g. cymoxanil+mancozeb, dimethomorph, or metalaxyl) upon disease appearance. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Plant blight-resistant varieties (e.g., Kufri Girdhari, Kufri Himalini, Kufri Jyoti).
Use only certified disease-free seed tubers.
potato_late_blight.source_note: CPRI Shimla Technical Bulletin on Potato Late Blight Management.

symptoms: Vigorous green foliage with even leaf expansion.
Clean stems free of brown necrosis or water-soaking.
Normal flowering and healthy underground tuberization.
potato_healthy.cause: No pathogen detected; healthy physiological status.
cultural_controls: Maintain deep earthing up around plants to encourage tuber bulking and prevent greening.
Keep ridges weed-free.
biological_controls: Preventive biofertilizer (Azotobacter, Phosphobacteria) application.
Neem cake incorporation in soil.
monitoring: Regular weekly field walk-throughs checking leaf undersides and soil moisture.
Inspect for aphid vectors on leaf undersides.
water_management: Maintain 65-75% available soil moisture during stolon formation and tuber bulking.
Withhold irrigation 10-15 days before harvest.
potato_healthy.chemical_advisory: No chemicals required. Continue standard balanced plant nutrition. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Ensure balanced potassium application for skin set and disease resistance.
Use healthy certified seed tubers.
potato_healthy.source_note: CPRI Potato Production Manual & National Horticulture Board India.

symptoms: Small, circular or irregular water-soaked spots on leaves.
Lesions enlarge to 3-5 mm, turning dark brown with a distinct yellow halo.
Leaves turn yellow and shed, causing severe defoliation and sunburn to fruit.
Warty, raised, scab-like spots on green bell peppers.
cultural_controls: Never enter or cultivate fields when pepper leaves are wet from rain or dew.
Destroy and plow down infected residues immediately post-harvest.
Disinfect nursery trays, tools, and stakes with a registered sterilant.
biological_controls: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens bio-agent.
Foliar bio-control sprays containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
monitoring: Regularly inspect the underside of bell pepper leaves for water-soaked greasy lesions.
Check seedlings in the nursery before transplanting.
water_management: Switch to drip irrigation to prevent bacterial dispersal via water droplets.
Avoid excess moisture around plant crowns.
pepper_bacterial_spot.chemical_advisory: Copper hydroxide mixed with protective mancozeb spray provides preventive suppression. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Plant resistant pepper varieties (races 1-5 resistance where available).
Use certified pathogen-free seeds treated with hot water (50°C for 25 min).
pepper_bacterial_spot.source_note: World Vegetable Center Capsicum IPM Series & ICAR-IIHR.

symptoms: Glossy, deep green leaves with crisp texture and no chlorosis.
Sturdy upright branches supporting flowers and developing fruits.
Smooth fruit surfaces free of scabs, sunscald, or rot.
pepper_healthy.cause: No pathogen detected; healthy crop condition.
cultural_controls: Maintain organic mulching to regulate soil temperature and conserve moisture.
Keep field borders clear of alternate solanaceous weeds.
biological_controls: Periodic application of vermicompost enriched with Trichoderma.
Encourage beneficial predators for thrips and mite suppression.
monitoring: Routine weekly scouting for early insect vector activity (aphids, mites, thrips).
Monitor soil moisture at 15 cm depth.
water_management: Deliver consistent drip irrigation to prevent blossom-end rot and plant stress.
Ensure efficient bed drainage during monsoon showers.
pepper_healthy.chemical_advisory: No chemicals needed. Continue organic nutrition and preventive care. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) before applying any chemical treatment.
prevention: Apply calcium and potassium to build thick, resilient cell walls.
Stake heavy fruiting plants to prevent lodging.
pepper_healthy.source_note: FAO Bell Pepper Production Guide & ICAR Extension Bulletin.

symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety lesions on leaf surfaces
Cracked, scabby brown fruit spots
apple_apple_scab.cause: Venturia inaequalis fungus spreading via airborne ascospores during wet spring.
cultural_controls: Rake and shred fallen apple leaves to reduce overwintering inoculum
Prune trees to open up the canopy for sunlight and air flow
biological_controls: Bio-fungicide sprays containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
Sulfur and potassium bicarbonate sprays
monitoring: Scout leaves early season right from green tip to petal fall
water_management: Avoid overhead sprinkling; utilize drip irrigation.
apple_apple_scab.chemical_advisory: If high infection pressure occurs, protectant fungicides like captan or dodine may be used according to local agricultural university advisory. Consult KVK.
prevention: Plant resistant cultivars such as Liberty, Prima, or Enterprise.

symptoms: Frog-eye leaf spots with purple borders
Black rotting mummified fruit on tree branches
cultural_controls: Prune dead twigs, fire-blight cankers, and remove all mummified apples.
biological_controls: Trichoderma viride applications during pruning season.
monitoring: Inspect orchards post-bloom for frog-eye leaf lesions.
water_management: Ensure proper orchard drainage and avoid canopy soaking.
apple_black_rot.chemical_advisory: Apply broad-spectrum protective fungicides during bloom if history exists. Consult KVK.
prevention: Maintain balanced tree vigor without excess nitrogen.

symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surfaces
Tube-like aecia structures on underside of leaves
apple_cedar_apple_rust.cause: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae requiring alternate host Juniper.
cultural_controls: Remove nearby wild junipers/red cedars within 1-2 km radius if feasible.
biological_controls: Liquid copper octanoate at bud break.
monitoring: Scout in spring when orange gelatinous galls appear on junipers.
water_management: Prevent lingering leaf wetness during early spring rains.
apple_cedar_apple_rust.chemical_advisory: Sterol inhibitors or mancozeb prior to rain events during pink to petal fall. Consult KVK.
prevention: Plant rust-immune or resistant varieties.

symptoms: Lush green, unblemished foliage with optimal chlorophyll density.
apple_healthy.cause: None. Plant is healthy and vigorous.
cultural_controls: Maintain balanced nitrogen-potassium fertilization and weed-free tree basin.
biological_controls: Periodic compost tea application to support beneficial phyllosphere microbes.
monitoring: Continue routine weekly orchard scouting.
water_management: Maintain drip irrigation matching tree evapo-transpiration.
prevention: Regular orchard sanitation and pruning.

symptoms: Reddish-brown narrow streaks parallel to leaf veins, expanding into black necrotic patches
Premature bunch ripening and severe leaf collapse
cultural_controls: De-leafing: surgically cut and remove necrotic leaf sections weekly; burn or bury infected leaves
Ensure wide planting spacing (2.0m x 2.0m) to promote fast canopy drying
biological_controls: Bio-agents like Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L) and Bacillus subtilis foliar spray
Neem oil 1% formulation with surfactant
monitoring: Track youngest leaf spotted (YLS) index weekly.
water_management: Provide good field drainage; avoid stagnant irrigation water around mats.
banana_black_sigatoka.chemical_advisory: Systemic triazoles or strobilurins rotated with mineral oil according to FRAC anti-resistance rules. Consult KVK.
prevention: Utilize tissue-culture plantlets from certified disease-free nurseries.
banana_black_sigatoka.source_note: NRCB (National Research Centre for Banana) Trichy IPM Advisory.

symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaf margins progressing inward
Petiole buckling and skirt of dead leaves clinging to pseudostem
Vascular discoloration (red-brown ring) inside pseudostem
banana_panama_wilt.cause: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (Foc TR4 / Race 1) soil-borne chlamydospores.
cultural_controls: Immediate eradication and quarantine of infected mats with quicklime treatment
Disinfect footwear and farming implements with 5% sodium hypochlorite
biological_controls: Soil application of Trichoderma reesei enriched farmyard manure at planting
monitoring: Scout fields for characteristic lower leaf collapse and split pseudostems.
water_management: Prevent runoff irrigation from infected parcels to clean parcels.
banana_panama_wilt.chemical_advisory: No curative chemical. Strict quarantine and soil biocontrol.
prevention: Adopt tolerant cultivars like Grand Naine with bio-priming.

symptoms: Broad, glossy emerald leaves with strong erect petioles.
cultural_controls: Desuckering: maintain mother plant and one healthy follower ratoon sucker.
biological_controls: Apply vesicular arbuscular mycorrhiza (VAM) and biofertilizers at root zone.
monitoring: Scout for aphid vectors and Sigatoka streaks every fortnight.
water_management: Maintain soil moisture around 70% field capacity.
prevention: Mulch banana basin with crop residue to conserve moisture.

symptoms: Sudden daytime wilting of plant while leaves remain green
Milky bacterial ooze stream when cut stem is placed in clear water
brinjal_bacterial_wilt.cause: Ralstonia solanacearum soil bacterium entering through root wounds.
cultural_controls: Uproot and burn wilted plants; drench planting pit with bleaching powder (2g/L)
Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (maize, sorghum)
biological_controls: Seedling root dip in Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L) before transplanting
monitoring: Look for sudden midday drooping in patches across the field.
water_management: Avoid furrow irrigation that carries bacterial runoff across rows.
brinjal_bacterial_wilt.chemical_advisory: Drench affected root zones with copper oxychloride (3g/L) + streptocycline (100ppm). Consult KVK.
prevention: Use wilt-resistant rootstocks for grafting or resistant varieties like Pant Rituraj.

symptoms: Circular buff to brown spots on leaves containing minute black pycnidia
Sunken, dry rotting lesions on brinjal fruits
cultural_controls: Collect and burn infected leaves and fallen fruit mummies
Deep summer plowing to bury resting mycelium
biological_controls: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum (5g/L) or neem formulation.
monitoring: Inspect lower leaves and developing fruit calyx during wet humid spells.
water_management: Use drip irrigation to keep fruit and foliage dry.
brinjal_phomopsis_blight.chemical_advisory: Foliar spray of mancozeb (2.5g/L) or carbendazim (1g/L) at fruit set. Consult KVK.
prevention: Sow certified pathogen-free seeds treated with Trichoderma.

symptoms: Vibrant lobed green leaves without mottling or necrosis; healthy purple/white flower buds.
cultural_controls: Maintain balanced NPK fertilization and staking for heavy fruiting.
biological_controls: Install yellow sticky traps for whitefly and shoot borer monitoring.
monitoring: Weekly scouting for shoot and fruit borer damage.
water_management: Provide uniform drip irrigation avoiding waterlogging.
prevention: Mulch beds with straw to prevent weed competition.

symptoms: Circular sunken lesions on green or ripe fruits with concentric rings of salmon-pink acervuli
Small circular necrotic spots on leaves and dieback of twigs from top downward
chilli_anthracnose.cause: Colletotrichum capsici and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides fungal complex.
cultural_controls: Remove and destroy infected fruits and dieback twigs during weeding
Avoid harvesting in morning dew; dry pods immediately after picking
biological_controls: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L) or Bacillus subtilis
5% NSKE (Neem Seed Kernel Extract) spray
monitoring: Inspect fruit ripening stage and twig tips during monsoon rain breaks.
water_management: Avoid overhead irrigation which splashes fungal spores.
chilli_anthracnose.chemical_advisory: Protective spray of copper oxychloride (3g/L) or azoxystrobin (1ml/L) at fruit formation. Consult KVK.
prevention: Treat seeds with Trichoderma viride (4g/kg) before sowing.

symptoms: Small water-soaked blisters turning brown with yellow halos
Severe defoliation leading to sun-scald on exposed fruits
cultural_controls: Promptly rogue out infected seedlings from nursery beds.
biological_controls: Bacillus subtilis foliar application at vegetative stage.
monitoring: Scout nursery and field every 4 days after heavy rainfall.
water_management: Shift to drip; avoid field work while plants are damp.
chilli_bacterial_leaf_spot.chemical_advisory: Foliar spray of copper hydroxide (2g/L) + streptocycline (100ppm). Consult KVK.
prevention: Hot water seed treatment (50C for 25 min) or certified seeds.

symptoms: Glossy dark green lanceolate leaves with vigorous branching and abundant flowering.
cultural_controls: Maintain balanced fertilisation with micronutrients (Zinc, Boron).
biological_controls: Install blue and yellow sticky traps for thrips and aphid monitoring.
monitoring: Weekly check for thrips leaf curling and mite webs.
water_management: Irrigate when top 2-3 cm soil is dry.
prevention: Maintain clean weed-free borders around chili beds.

symptoms: Rectangular brown to tan lesions restricted between leaf veins
Lesions coalesce to cause severe blighting of maize canopy
corn_cercospora_leaf_spot.cause: Cercospora zeae-maydis fungal pathogen surviving on corn stover.
cultural_controls: Tillage to bury corn residue in continuous maize fields
Two-year crop rotation with soybean or legumes
biological_controls: Bio-formulations of Bacillus pumilus or Trichoderma.
monitoring: Scout lower leaves starting at V8 to tasseling stage.
water_management: Ensure proper drainage and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
corn_cercospora_leaf_spot.chemical_advisory: Strobilurin or triazole fungicides applied at tasseling (VT) stage if threshold crossed. Consult KVK.
prevention: Select hybrid corn varieties with high Gray Leaf Spot resistance.
corn_cercospora_leaf_spot.source_note: ICAR-IIMR (Indian Institute of Maize Research) Advisory.

symptoms: Oval to elongate cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture epidermal tissue releasing powdery spores
corn_common_rust.cause: Puccinia sorghi fungus spreading by windborne urediniospores.
cultural_controls: Early planting to escape late-season heavy spore showers.
biological_controls: Bio-fungicide sprays of Trichoderma viride.
monitoring: Inspect corn leaves during cool, foggy morning conditions.
water_management: Avoid overhead irrigation in cool temperatures.
corn_common_rust.chemical_advisory: Foliar spray of mancozeb (2g/L) or propiconazole (1ml/L) if >6 pustules per leaf before silking. Consult KVK.
prevention: Plant resistant hybrids with Rp gene rust protection.

symptoms: Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2 to 15 cm long)
Dark olive fuzz of spores visible inside lesions under damp weather
cultural_controls: Crop rotation out of maize for 1 to 2 years; residue shredding.
biological_controls: Pseudomonas fluorescens foliar spray.
monitoring: Scout lower leaves prior to tasseling.
water_management: Maintain adequate row spacing (60cm x 20cm) for ventilation.
corn_northern_leaf_blight.chemical_advisory: Foliar application of azoxystrobin + tebuconazole if lesions appear before silking. Consult KVK.
prevention: Choose resistant maize hybrids.

symptoms: Broad deep-green leaves with sturdy stalks and well-developed brace roots.
cultural_controls: Split application of nitrogen at basal, knee-high (V6), and tasseling.
biological_controls: Pheromone traps for fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) monitoring.
monitoring: Scout weekly for fall armyworm whorl damage.
water_management: Critical irrigation at knee-high, tasseling, and silking stages.
prevention: Balanced fertilisation including zinc sulphate.

symptoms: Water-soaked angular leaf spots bounded by veinlets
Black lesions along main veins (black arm) and sunken water-soaked spots on bolls
cotton_bacterial_blight.cause: Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum seed and residue borne bacterium.
cultural_controls: Acid delinting of cotton seeds; destroy infected plant debris.
biological_controls: Seed bacterization with Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/kg).
monitoring: Scout 30-45 days after sowing during monsoon rains.
water_management: Avoid water stagnation in furrows; ensure field drainage.
cotton_bacterial_blight.chemical_advisory: Spray copper oxychloride (2.5g/L) + streptocycline (100ppm). Consult KVK.
prevention: Plant immune or resistant cotton varieties.
cotton_bacterial_blight.source_note: CICR (Central Institute for Cotton Research) Nagpur Advisory.

symptoms: Yellowing and browning along leaf margins progressing inward
Petiole and leaf drop starting from bottom; dark brown ring in stem vascular xylem
cotton_fusarium_wilt.cause: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum soil-inhabiting fungus.
cultural_controls: Deep summer ploughing; crop rotation with non-host cereals (pearl millet, sorghum).
biological_controls: Apply Trichoderma harzianum enriched farmyard manure (2.5 kg/ton).
monitoring: Scout at squaring and flowering stage for patchy wilting.
water_management: Avoid over-irrigation in heavy black cotton soils.
cotton_fusarium_wilt.chemical_advisory: Soil drenching with carbendazim (1g/L) at initial symptom onset. Consult KVK.
prevention: Use wilt-resistant cotton cultivars.

symptoms: Robust dark green palmate leaves with vigorous sympodial branching and healthy squares.
cultural_controls: Timely inter-cultivation and balanced nitrogen management to prevent rank growth.
biological_controls: Install yellow sticky traps for sucking pest monitoring (jassids, whiteflies).
monitoring: Scout weekly for pink bollworm and sucking pest thresholds.
water_management: Provide drip irrigation at square formation and boll development.
prevention: Adhere to recommended spacing.

symptoms: Circular reddish-brown leaf spots with dark margins and tiny black pycnidia
Berries turn brown, shrivel into hard, black wrinkled mummies
cultural_controls: Remove all mummified berries from vines and ground during winter pruning
Canopy management: shoot positioning and leaf removal around fruit zone for airflow
biological_controls: Foliar bio-fungicide sprays of Bacillus subtilis.
monitoring: Inspect vines from bud break through 4 weeks post-bloom.
water_management: Use drip under vine row; avoid overhead watering.
grape_black_rot.chemical_advisory: Protective fungicide (mancozeb or kresoxim-methyl) before rainfall events. Consult KVK.
prevention: Prune to open trellis structure.
grape_black_rot.source_note: NRCG (National Research Centre for Grapes) Pune IPM.

symptoms: Tiger-stripe leaf pattern: interveinal yellow and necrotic brown bands with green veins
Dark purple/black speckling on berry skins (measles)
grape_esca_black_measles.cause: Fungal trunk disease complex (Phaeomoniella chlamydospora, Phaeoacremonium minimum, Fomitiporia).
cultural_controls: Prune late in dormant season; seal all pruning wounds with wound sealant or fungicide paste
Mark diseased vines and prune them last to avoid transmitting fungus via shears
biological_controls: Treat pruning wounds immediately with Trichoderma-based bio-paste.
monitoring: Scout for tiger-stripe foliar symptoms in mid-summer.
water_management: Avoid water stress during fruit sizing.
grape_esca_black_measles.chemical_advisory: No cure once inside trunk. Trunk renewal or surgical removal of rotted wood. Consult KVK.
prevention: Plant certified disease-free vine nursery stock.

symptoms: Large irregular brown patches with darker borders on mature foliage
Premature defoliation resulting in berry sun-scald and poor sugar accumulation
cultural_controls: Remove and destroy infected leaf litter beneath vines.
biological_controls: Neem seed oil spray or Trichoderma viride.
monitoring: Scout post-monsoon during fruit veraison.
water_management: Maintain drip irrigation.
grape_leaf_blight.chemical_advisory: Spray copper oxychloride (2.5g/L) or azoxystrobin (1ml/L). Consult KVK.
prevention: Ensure adequate ventilation through canopy thinning.

symptoms: Lush broad green leaves with healthy tendrils and clean developing clusters.
cultural_controls: Proper canopy shoot thinning and berry thinning for uniform cluster density.
biological_controls: Beneficial cover crops (clover, vetch) between vine rows.
monitoring: Weekly scouting for downy and powdery mildew signs.
water_management: Regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) post-veraison to enhance fruit quality.
prevention: Sanitary pruning practices.

symptoms: Water-soaked stripes starting from leaf tips and margins with wavy edges
Lesions turn yellow to straw-white; bacterial amber beads on morning leaves
cultural_controls: Drain excess field water temporarily; avoid high nitrogen top-dressing during disease spread
Maintain clean bunds free of weed hosts (Leersia oryzoides)
biological_controls: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L) or Bacillus subtilis.
monitoring: Inspect field during tillering to panicle initiation after windy storms.
water_management: Avoid deep standing water; practice alternate wetting and drying (AWD).
rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.chemical_advisory: Spray copper hydroxide (2g/L) + streptocycline (100ppm). Consult KVK.
prevention: Grow BLB-resistant varieties like Improved Samba Mahsuri or Pusa Basmati 1718.
rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.source_note: ICAR-IIRR (Indian Institute of Rice Research) Hyderabad Advisory.

symptoms: Oval or circular brown lesions with yellow halo evenly scattered over leaves
Dark brown spots on glumes causing grain discoloration and unfilled grains
rice_brown_spot.cause: Bipolaris oryzae fungal pathogen commonly associated with nutrient-deficient soils.
cultural_controls: Apply balanced fertilizers including potash and silicon; correct soil zinc and iron deficiencies
Treat seeds with hot water (53-54C for 10-12 min)
biological_controls: Seed treatment and foliar spray with Trichoderma viride.
monitoring: Scout seedlings in nursery and field from tillering onwards.
water_management: Prevent water stress in rainfed lowland or upland rice.
rice_brown_spot.chemical_advisory: Foliar spray of mancozeb (2g/L) or edifenphos (1ml/L). Consult KVK.
prevention: Soil amendment with silicon and organic matter.

symptoms: Spindle-shaped / diamond-shaped lesions with gray or whitish centers and brown margins
Neck blast: black necrotic collar at panicle base resulting in completely empty upright whiteheads
cultural_controls: Avoid excess nitrogen application; split nitrogen into 3-4 doses
Avoid late planting which exposes crop to cool dewy weather
biological_controls: Pseudomonas fluorescens seed treatment (10g/kg) and foliar spray (0.2%).
monitoring: Scout lower leaves during cloudy, drizzle weather with cool nights.
water_management: Maintain continuous shallow water layer (2-5cm) in blast-prone fields.
rice_leaf_blast.chemical_advisory: Foliar spray of tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6g/L) or isoprothiolane 40 EC (1.5ml/L) at boot leaf stage. Consult KVK.
prevention: Plant blast-resistant varieties.

symptoms: Erect, vibrant green tillers with clean flag leaves and healthy root crowns.
cultural_controls: Maintain balanced NPK + Zinc sulphate (25 kg/ha basal).
biological_controls: Encourage dragonflies and spiders as natural pest predators in paddy.
monitoring: Monitor for stem borer dead hearts and leaf folder foldings.
water_management: Adopt Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) to save water.
prevention: Certified disease-free seed sourcing.

symptoms: Small round to oval orange-brown pustules scattered randomly across upper leaf blade
Leaves turn prematurely chlorotic and die back
cultural_controls: Timely sowing before mid-November in North Indian plains to escape temperature rise.
biological_controls: Foliar spray of bio-formulations of Trichoderma.
monitoring: Inspect flag leaves starting from January to February.
water_management: Avoid evening irrigations that keep canopy moist through the night.
wheat_brown_rust.chemical_advisory: Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) or tebuconazole (1ml/L) upon detecting initial pustules. Consult KVK.
prevention: Cultivate resistant varieties like DBW 187, DBW 222, or HD 3226.
wheat_brown_rust.source_note: ICAR-IIWBR (Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research) Karnal Advisory.

symptoms: Bright yellow/lemon-yellow pustules arranged in continuous narrow stripes between leaf veins
Powdery yellow dust rubs off onto fingers readily
wheat_yellow_rust.cause: Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici thriving under cool dewy conditions.
cultural_controls: Eradicate alternate host barberry shrubs near fields in sub-mountainous zones.
biological_controls: Bio-priming with Trichoderma.
monitoring: Early scouting in foothill regions (Punjab, Haryana, J&K, HP) in December-January.
water_management: Prevent lingering water droplets in canopy.
wheat_yellow_rust.chemical_advisory: Spray propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) immediately upon noticing initial foci/yellow patches. Consult KVK.
prevention: Plant stripe-rust resistant cultivars like HD 3086 or PBW 725.

symptoms: Irregular rectangular chlorotic-necrotic leaf blotches with prominent black specks (pycnidia)
cultural_controls: Crop rotation and stubble incorporation.
biological_controls: Bacillus subtilis sprays.
monitoring: Scout lower leaves during rainy vegetative stage.
water_management: Ensure field drainage.
wheat_septoria.chemical_advisory: Triazole or SDHI fungicides if flag leaf is threatened. Consult KVK.
prevention: Use clean seed and resistant cultivars.

symptoms: Uniform emerald foliage with healthy tillering and erect flag leaves.
cultural_controls: Apply recommended NPK (120:60:40) with split urea application.
biological_controls: Seed inoculation with Azotobacter and PSB bio-fertilizers.
monitoring: Scout for aphid colonies and rust signs weekly.
water_management: Ensure 5-6 critical irrigations: Crown root initiation (CRI), tillering, jointing, flowering, milk, and dough stages.
prevention: Optimum sowing window (first fortnight of November).

symptoms: General pale yellowing (chlorosis) starting on older lower leaves and moving up
Stunted plant growth, thin spindly stems, and reduced fruit size
tomato_nutrient_deficiency_nitrogen.cause: Insufficient available soil nitrogen (NO3- / NH4+) or severe leaching.
cultural_controls: Apply well-decomposed farmyard manure or vermicompost to root zone
Incorporate green manure leguminous crops (dhaincha, sunnhemp) in crop rotation
biological_controls: Inoculate soil with Azospirillum or Azotobacter bio-fertilizers.
monitoring: Monitor lower leaf color during vegetative and early flowering stage.
water_management: Avoid excessive irrigation that leaches mobile nitrate below root zone.
tomato_nutrient_deficiency_nitrogen.chemical_advisory: Foliar spray of 1% to 2% urea solution or fertigation with calcium nitrate (5g/L). Consult KVK.
prevention: Soil testing before planting to calculate precise nitrogen demand.

symptoms: Dull dark green leaves developing purple or bronze pigmentation on undersides and margins
Stunted root growth, delayed tuber bulking, and small tubers with internal rust spots
potato_nutrient_deficiency_phosphorus.cause: Soil phosphorus fixation in acidic or calcareous soils; low available orthophosphate.
cultural_controls: Apply organic matter and compost to improve phosphorus mobility and reduce fixation
biological_controls: Soil application of Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria (PSB) and mycorrhizal fungi (VAM).
monitoring: Inspect young plants at stolon initiation.
water_management: Maintain consistent soil moisture to facilitate phosphorus diffusion to roots.
potato_nutrient_deficiency_phosphorus.chemical_advisory: Foliar application of 0.5% mono-potassium phosphate (0:52:34) or single super phosphate basal application. Consult KVK.
prevention: Soil test based banded phosphorus placement near seed tuber.
potato_nutrient_deficiency_phosphorus.source_note: CPRI (Central Potato Research Institute) Shimla Advisory.

symptoms: Cupping and distortion of young leaves with scorched margins
Water-soaked sunken black leathery rot at the blossom end of pepper fruits
pepper_nutrient_deficiency_calcium.cause: Low calcium uptake driven by fluctuating soil moisture, high salinity, or excess nitrogen/potassium.
cultural_controls: Mulch beds to maintain steady soil moisture levels; avoid soil drying between waterings
biological_controls: Apply humic acid to stimulate root hair calcium uptake.
monitoring: Inspect fruit blossom ends 10-14 days after flower petal drop.
water_management: Provide uniform, consistent drip irrigation; avoid drought cycles.
pepper_nutrient_deficiency_calcium.chemical_advisory: Foliar spray of 0.5% calcium chloride or calcium nitrate directed at young foliage and fruit clusters. Consult KVK.
prevention: Apply gypsum or agricultural lime based on soil pH.
